[RT-1] High-frequency client publish => unbounded fan-out
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: NetcodeController publishes position and animation every 100ms (two separate publishData calls per tick) from every client using LiveKit data channels, with no server-side rate limiting or batching. There is no sequence/timestamp/replay logic so every client sends full updates continually.  
Impact: As participants grow, messages/sec and fan-out multiply (client_count * ~20 msgs/sec * recipients) causing bandwidth/CPU explosion on the RTC service and likely dropped messages, high latency, or service exhaustion.  
Fix: Reduce and/or batch updates (coalesce position+animation), lower send frequency, add client-side dampening and server-side per-client and per-room rate limits before allowing publish.

File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)

There is no sequence/timestamp/replay logic so every client sends full updates continually.  
Impact: As participants grow, messages/sec and fan-out multiply (client_count * ~20 msgs/sec * recipients) causing bandwidth/CPU explosion on the RTC service and likely dropped messages, high latency, or service exhaustion.

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-2] Token issuance ignores current room occupancy
File: src/pages/api/universe/connection.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: The connection endpoint issues LiveKit access tokens granting roomJoin/canPublish without checking live participant counts or enforcing a room participant limit; token creation is unconditional.  
Impact: Clients can obtain tokens and join rooms beyond intended capacity, enabling the unbounded fan-out from RT-1 and risking rapid resource exhaustion of the RTC cluster.  
Fix: Query LiveKit (RoomServiceClient) for current participant count and enforce per-room caps/deny-or-queue token issuance, or embed scoped TTLs/leases to control join rate.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-3] Webhook handlers perform synchronous DB writes per event
File: src/app/api/webhooks/livekit/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: LiveKit webhook handling does immediate Prisma updates (increment/decrement currentUsers and isLive flags) on each room/participant event with no batching, buffering, or backoff.  
Impact: High churn (many joins/leaves) can create DB write storms, increased latency or failed webhook processing, and stale/incorrect counters under load.  
Fix: Buffer/debounce or batch counter updates (Redis counters, background worker, or idempotent queue) and make webhook processing fast/async.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-4] No adaptive backpressure / slow-client handling on publishes
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: publishData is awaited but no timeouts, retries, drop policy, or adaptive rate reduction exist; only single-send locks prevent concurrent sends. There are no sequence numbers or ACKs to detect lost/missed updates.  
Impact: Slow or congested clients can block publish calls or generate stale state after reconnects, increasing perceived drops and inconsistent remote state.  
Fix: Add publish timeouts, drop/skip stale updates, include sequence/timestamp metadata, and implement adaptive send rates based on connectionState/RTT.

--- INFO ---

[RT-5] LiveKit used as managed realtime provider (with fallback)
File: src/lib/livekit.ts
Evidence: The repo uses livekit-server-sdk/room service and provides a fallback/mock when the LiveKit service is unavailable.
